### Color swatches
Pick one color from a preset palette, on native radio buttons.

Component ID: `color-swatches`

#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `css-only`. No dedicated entry in the reviewed Google component inventory.

Example: Eight label colors for a calendar are color swatches. Any brand color a designer types in is the native color input.

Relationship: none. Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

Requirements and boundaries: design reference web-extensions-review. The inventory page renders client-side, so this review relies on the 2026-09-13 inventory review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.

Support (2026-10-18, `llm.md#color-swatches`): A fieldset of native radios drawn as round chips of their colors, a ring around the checked one, the shared focus ring, a 48px target and an optional native color input for a custom value.

Web adaptation: Native radios keep one Tab stop, arrow keys and form submission; each swatch is named by visually hidden text in its label.

Known boundary: Swatch color, size and shape, the checked ring, the group name, arrow keys, the form value, the focus ring after arrow keys and the swatch color under forced colors are checked in Chromium; other engines, spoken output and enlarged text remain unverified.

Full parity remains unassessed. [Capability evidence](../references/capability-roadmap.md#color-swatches).

#### Contract

A `<fieldset class="color-swatches">` holds a `<legend>` and one radio per color, each in a `<label>` whose visually hidden text ("Purple") comes before the radio, with `--md-comp-color-swatch-color` set on the radio. The radio is drawn as a 40px round chip of that color with a 48px target, and the checked one gets a ring, so the choice is marked by shape as well as color. Tab, the arrow keys and form submission stay native. Add an `<input type="color">` in a label of its own at the end for a custom value; it is already drawn as a matching round swatch. Under forced colors the swatches keep their colors and the checked one gets a `Highlight` outline. CSS only; there is no JavaScript.

#### Syntax

```html
<fieldset class="color-swatches">
  <legend>Label color</legend>
  <label><span class="visually-hidden">Purple</span><input type="radio" name="label-color" value="#6750a4" style="--md-comp-color-swatch-color: #6750a4" checked></label>
  <label><span class="visually-hidden">Green</span><input type="radio" name="label-color" value="#386a20" style="--md-comp-color-swatch-color: #386a20"></label>
  <label><span class="visually-hidden">Red</span><input type="radio" name="label-color" value="#b3261e" style="--md-comp-color-swatch-color: #b3261e"></label>
  <label><span class="visually-hidden">Custom color</span><input type="color" name="label-color-custom" value="#ff8800"></label>
</fieldset>
```

#### Also documented

The Color swatches section of the [API reference](https://www.expressivecss.com/llm.md) also covers Tokens.

#### Rules

- `color-swatches-is-a-fieldset`: A .color-swatches is a <fieldset> with a <legend>, so the radios read as one named group.
- `color-swatch-is-named`: A swatch shows no text, so name each radio with visually hidden text in its label, such as "Purple".
